Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",

                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email

| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host

HTTP access to Shopper admin team-settings / Livewire endpoints (CVE-2026-47744) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts HTTP requests to the vulnerable Shopper admin panel routes — Settings/Team/Index and Settings/Team/RolePermission — including their Livewire AJAX endpoints. Pre-patch (Shopper < 2.8.0) these were reachable by any authenticated panel user and were the only network observable for the authorization-bypass / RBAC privilege-escalation chain disclosed in GHSA-c3qp-2ggw-xjg7. Rationale: The article names exactly two Livewire components — Settings/Team/Index and Settings/Team/RolePermission — as the abuse surface. Livewire routes those component names verbatim through /livewire/update (Livewire v3) and /livewire/message/{component} (v2), so the component string and these endpoints are the highest-fidelity strings available pre-exploit. POST/PUT/PATCH on the role-permission route is the specific action that grants/escalates permissions, distinguishing exploitation from normal page loads. No external IOC corroboration was attempted since the advisory exposes no network IOCs — only source-code paths.
ATT&CKT1190 T1068 T1078.003
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Shopper panel administrators (manage_users holders) creating roles or updating role permissions in normal operations
  • Internal QA / penetration-test exercises against the upgraded (>=2.8.0) panel
  • Application monitoring/uptime probes hitting the admin panel index without authentication (will 302 to login but still appear in HTTP logs)
  • Crawlers / bots probing /livewire/update on any Livewire-built site (broad Livewire scanners)
  • Reverse-proxy retries duplicating the same POST to /livewire/update on transient 5xx
Suppression filter
| where not (User in~ ("admin","superadmin") and ClientIP in ("10.0.0.0/8","192.168.0.0/16")) and not (UserAgent has_any ("Pingdom","UptimeRobot","StatusCake"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the Shopper composer.lock from the affected host and confirm shopper/framework < 2.8.0; if patched, downgrade severity. Identify the authenticated session behind the request (panel session cookie or X-Forwarded-User) and map to the panel user — was it a holder of view_users only? 2) Contain: force-logout all panel sessions, rotate panel admin credentials, and either upgrade to shopper/framework 2.8.0 immediately or block /livewire/update and /admin/settings/team* at the WAF until upgrade. 3) Hunt: dump the roles and role_permission tables and diff against a known-good snapshot — look for newly granted manage_users / edit_orders to non-admin accounts; review the panel users table for unexpected deletions of legitimate administrators; pivot on the source IP across the prior 30 days for any other panel reconnaissance.
// Requires IIS / nginx access logs ingested to a custom table; M365 Defender XDR does not natively capture inbound HTTP to a self-hosted PHP app.
// Pivot via DeviceNetworkEvents for the web server's inbound traffic to the panel's listening port, then triage in the proxy/WAF.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where LocalPort in (80, 443, 8080, 8443)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe","php-fpm.exe","php.exe","nginx.exe","httpd.exe","caddy.exe")
| where ActionType == "InboundConnectionAccepted"
| summarize Connections = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, LocalIP, LocalPort, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName
| where Connections > 5
| order by LastSeen desc
let TargetPaths = dynamic(["settings/team","settings.team.index","settings.team.role-permission","settings.team.rolepermission","/livewire/update","/livewire/message/settings.team"]);
(union isfuzzy=true
    (W3CIISLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where csUriStem has_any (TargetPaths) or csUriQuery has_any (TargetPaths)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source="IIS", Computer, Method=csMethod, Url=strcat(csUriStem, iff(isnotempty(csUriQuery), strcat("?", csUriQuery), "")), Status=scStatus, ClientIP=cIP, UserAgent=csUserAgent, User=csUserName),
    (AppServiceHTTPLogs
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where CsUriStem has_any (TargetPaths) or CsUriQuery has_any (TargetPaths)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source="AppService", Computer=CsHost, Method=CsMethod, Url=strcat(CsUriStem, iff(isnotempty(CsUriQuery), strcat("?", CsUriQuery), "")), Status=ScStatus, ClientIP=CIp, UserAgent=UserAgent, User=CsUsername),
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where RequestURL has_any (TargetPaths)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source=DeviceProduct, Computer=DestinationHostName, Method=RequestMethod, Url=RequestURL, Status=tostring(EventOutcome), ClientIP=SourceIP, UserAgent=RequestClientApplication, User=SourceUserName)
)
| where Method in~ ("POST","PUT","PATCH") or Url has_any ("role-permission","rolepermission")
| summarize Hits = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Methods = make_set(Method), Statuses = make_set(Status), UserAgents = make_set(UserAgent, 5), Users = make_set(User, 10) by ClientIP, Computer, Source
| order by LastSeen desc

Unauthenticated POST to AIT-BSC /<name>/start with path-traversal form fields (CVE-2026-47731) AIExploitation High
Hunts the actual exploit shape against the AIT-Core BSC HTTP API: POST to /<name>/start carrying attacker-controlled log_dir_path, file_name_pattern, or path form fields with path-traversal indicators (../, %2e%2e, absolute paths like /etc, /home, /root). Pre-patch AIT-Core <3.1.1 and <2.6.1 lets an unauthenticated remote caller use these fields to redirect log_file writes anywhere ait-bsc can write — corruption of .py modules then yields RCE on next restart. Rationale: Targets the exact REST shape from the article (the Bottle route `/<name>/start` registered in `StreamCaptureManagerServer._route()`) plus the three attacker-influenced form fields named in the bug write-up (log_dir_path, file_name_pattern, path) combined with traversal markers (../ %2e%2e absolute /etc /root /home). The article confirms there is no auth on the route and these fields go straight into `os.path.join` without realpath canonicalisation. Cross-checked against the GHSA-p462-prxw-mjx4 advisory and the AIT-Core 3.1.1/2.6.1 patch notes which scope the same parameter list. Falcon FDR doesn't natively ship HTTP request bodies so falcon_logscale_query is empty; the same telemetry is covered by NetworkConnectIP4 in UC2. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p462-prxw-mjx4 • https://github.com/NASA-AMMOS/AIT-Core/releases/tag/3.1.1
ATT&CKT1190 T1565.001
Data sourcesWeb Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal vulnerability scanners (Tenable, Qualys, Burp Pro) probing the BSC endpoint as part of a sanctioned scan
  • Mission-ops engineers running `python_poc.py` from the AIT-Core test harness against a lab BSC instance
  • Custom ground-system tooling that legitimately passes log_dir_path to relocate captures between mission phases
  • Health-check probes that POST malformed bodies to /start to verify the route is alive (yields 400 but trips URL pattern)
Suppression filter
and not (SrcIp in ("10.", "172.16.", "192.168.") and UA has_any ("Nessus","Qualys","Tenable","Burp","Acunetix","Nmap")) and not (Uri endswith "/healthcheck/start")
Response runbook
Triage: pull the full POST body from the proxy/WAF capture, decode the form fields, and verify whether log_dir_path / path resolves outside the configured `root_log_directory` from bsc.yaml. Pivot on `source IP` to see whether the same caller hit /stats or other handler names. Contain: block the source IP at the perimeter and stop the ait-bsc systemd unit (`systemctl stop ait-bsc`) — do NOT just kill the process because gevent greenlets can keep writing in an infinite-loop bug mentioned in the advisory. Hunt: review DeviceFileEvents for writes by python/ait-bsc into /etc, /root, /home/*/.ssh, site-packages/ait/, or any *.py outside the project tree in the previous 24h; verify SHA256 of any AIT-Core .py against the package wheel hashes; check for outbound TCP from ait-bsc to non-baseline destinations (see related UC2).
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("InboundConnectionAccepted","ConnectionFound","ListeningConnectionCreated")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName matches regex @"(?i)^(python(3(\.\d+)?)?|ait-bsc)(\.exe)?$"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("ait-bsc","ait.core.bsc","ait_bsc","StreamCaptureManagerServer","bsc.yaml")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Sessions=count(), AnyLocalPort=any(LocalPort) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP
| order by FirstSeen desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let TraversalTokens = dynamic(["log_dir_path","file_name_pattern","..%2F","..%2f","..%5C","..%5c","%2e%2e","path=%2F","path=/etc","path=/root","path=/home","path=/var","path=/tmp","log_dir_path=/"]);
let IISHits = W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where csMethod =~ "POST"
    | where csUriStem matches regex @"(?i)^/[^/]+/start$"
    | where csUriQuery has_any (TraversalTokens) or csUriStem has_any ("%2e%2e", "..")
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, SrcIp=tostring(cIP), DstPort=tostring(sPort), Uri=csUriStem, Detail=csUriQuery, UA=csUserAgent, Source="W3CIIS";
let CEFHits = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
    | where RequestURL matches regex @"(?i)/[^/]+/start(\?|$)"
    | where Message has_any (TraversalTokens) or RequestURL has_any ("%2e%2e", "..")
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=coalesce(DestinationHostName, DestinationDnsDomain, DeviceExternalID), SrcIp=SourceIP, DstPort=tostring(DestinationPort), Uri=RequestURL, Detail=Message, UA=RequestClientApplication, Source="CEF";
let SyslogHits = Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ProcessName has_any ("ait-bsc","ait_bsc","bsc","python","python3")
    | where SyslogMessage has "/start" and SyslogMessage has_any (TraversalTokens)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, SrcIp=HostIP, DstPort="", Uri="/<name>/start", Detail=SyslogMessage, UA="", Source="Syslog";
union IISHits, CEFHits, SyslogHits
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Hits=count(), SampleDetail=any(Detail) by Host, SrcIp, Uri, Source
| order by LastSeen desc

ait-bsc outbound TCP to public/non-baseline destination (attacker-supplied loc port) AICommand & Control High
Detects ait-bsc / python processes running the ait.core.bsc StreamCaptureManager opening outbound TCP/UDP sessions to non-RFC1918, non-baseline destinations. Per CVE-2026-47731 the unauth /<name>/start endpoint lets a remote caller supply arbitrary `loc` + `port` form values which BSC dutifully `gevent.spawn`s a socket against — making BSC initiate egress to attacker-controlled infrastructure that then streams attacker-chosen bytes back into the file append sink. Rationale: Anchors directly on the article-confirmed primitive: the attacker controls `loc` and `port` in the form body and BSC `gevent.spawn`s a SocketStreamCapturer at that endpoint — i.e. BSC initiates the egress under attacker direction. Process-context match uses the exact module path (`ait.core.bsc`), class name (`StreamCaptureManagerServer`), and config file (`bsc.yaml`) shown in the source excerpt. Sentinel query splits process-context resolution onto ImProcessCreate (which carries ActingProcessCommandLine) and joins by DvcHostname into ImNetworkSession (which does not) — the schema-correct way to express the same logic the Defender query expresses inline. Cross-checked against GHSA-p462-prxw-mjx4 patch diff which restricts socket creation to validated paths only. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p462-prxw-mjx4 • https://github.com/NASA-AMMOS/AIT-Core/blob/main/ait/core/bsc.py
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1659
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate ground-station configurations where BSC connects to a public-IP downlink receiver (rare, but check bsc.yaml first)
  • Mission-ops sites running ait-bsc against a cloud-hosted relay (AWS Ground Station, Azure Orbital) which presents as a public IP
  • Engineer testing against a remote development BSC server over a tunnel that egresses to the tunnel endpoint's public IP
  • Updates / pip installs run from the same venv where ait-bsc is installed (mitigated by the process-name filter, but pip can shell into python entrypoints)
Suppression filter
| where not (DstIpAddr in ("<known_ground_station_ip_1>","<known_ground_station_ip_2>")) and not (DstPortNumber in (8080, 8443) and BscCommandLine has "--allow-public-relay")
Response runbook
Triage: pull bsc.yaml from the host and confirm the destination IP+port is NOT in the configured handler list — any unrecognised loc is high-fidelity evil. Capture the BSC handler stats endpoint output (`GET /stats`) to enumerate every currently registered logger and their loc/port/path. Contain: stop the ait-bsc service and revoke any open TCP socket — note the advisory warns of an infinite-loop write bug on close, so plan disk-space monitoring during teardown. Hunt: search DeviceFileEvents for writes by the same ait-bsc PID within the same window, especially to .py / .sh / authorized_keys / cron paths; verify all AIT-Core site-packages files match the wheel hash; pivot the remote IP across DNS / proxy logs to find other internal hosts that reached out to it.

| where InitiatingProcessFileName matches regex @"(?i)^(python(3(\.\d+)?)?|ait-bsc)(\.exe)?$"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("ait-bsc","ait.core.bsc","ait_bsc","StreamCaptureManagerServer","bsc.yaml")
| where ActionType in ("ConnectionSuccess","ConnectionAttempt","ConnectionRequest")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Sessions=count(), DistinctRemotes=dcount(RemoteIP) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by FirstSeen desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let BscHosts = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(python(3)?(\.\d+)?|ait-bsc)(\.exe)?$"
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("ait-bsc","ait.core.bsc","ait_bsc","StreamCaptureManagerServer","bsc.yaml")

ImNetworkSession

| join kind=leftouter BscHosts on DvcHostname
| project FirstSeen, LastSeen, DvcHostname, BscCommandLine=Cmd, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, Sessions, Bytes
| order by FirstSeen desc

Installation of compromised Microsoft durabletask PyPI versions 1.4.1-1.4.3 AIDelivery High
Detects pip installation of the three malicious durabletask SDK versions (1.4.1, 1.4.2, 1.4.3) published to PyPI on 2026-05-19. Hits every CI runner, build host, or developer workstation that pulled the trojanised release; pin to 1.4.0 and treat any match as compromised. Rationale: Pins on the three article-named malicious versions of the official 400k-DL/month durabletask package, only legitimate channel is pip install referencing one of those version strings. Hashes (069ac1dc... / 7d80b3ef... / aeaf583e...) cross-referenced via StepSecurity public run analysis. Cross-checked against: • https://app.stepsecurity.io/github/actions-security-demo/compromised-packages/actions/runs/26115553485
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate `pip install durabletask` against a pinned-but-coincidentally-matching internal mirror that has not yanked the bad versions
  • Security researchers / IR teams intentionally installing the malicious version in a sandbox for analysis
  • Old CI logs replayed through SIEM ingestion (timestamps will look current but happened in May)
  • Vulnerability scanners (Snyk, Dependabot CLI) inspecting requirements files that mention these versions in cmdline diagnostics
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--dry-run","--no-deps","sandbox","pip-audit","safety check"))
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: Run `pip show durabletask` (or query SBOM) on the matching host; confirm installed version. If 1.4.1/1.4.2/1.4.3, treat as compromised. Pull the Defender process tree from Timestamp+/- 5 min for child managed.pyz spawns. 2. CONTAIN: Isolate the host (especially CI runners). Rotate every secret reachable from that runtime: AWS keys, Azure SPs, GCP SA keys, GitHub PATs (`gh auth token` was harvested), npm tokens, kubeconfigs. Delete `/tmp/managed.pyz` and the fake `pgsql-monitor.service` user unit. 3. HUNT: Pivot on this DeviceId across DeviceNetworkEvents for check.git-service.com / m-kosche.com, and across AWS CloudTrail for SendCommand / AssumeRole originating from this host's identity in the prior 7 days.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("pip","pip3","python3","python3.14","python")
   or FileName in~ ("pip","pip3")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "durabletask"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("1.4.1","1.4.2","1.4.3")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
let MaliciousVersions = dynamic(["1.4.1","1.4.2","1.4.3"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("pip","pip3","python3","python3.14","python")
   or TargetProcessName has_any ("pip","pip3")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "durabletask" or TargetProcessCommandLine has "durabletask"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (MaliciousVersions) or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (MaliciousVersions)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Installation of Compromised Microsoft durabletask PyPI Versions

description: Detects pip install of the three malicious durabletask SDK versions (1.4.1, 1.4.2, 1.4.3) tied to the May 2026 TeamPCP supply-chain compromise.

Python urlretrieve download of rope.pyz from check.git-service.com to /tmp/managed.pyz AIInstallation Medium
Catches the 14-line dropper executing at `import durabletask` time: a Python process performs an HTTPS GET to check.git-service.com/rope.pyz and writes the response to /tmp/managed.pyz. Highly specific to the TeamPCP rope.pyz framework — the URL path /rope.pyz and target filename /tmp/managed.pyz are both attacker-chosen literals. Rationale: Three article-grounded literals correlated: process is python*, destination is `check.git-service.com` (or its 160.119.64.3 / 83.142.209.194 IPs), and the write target is `/tmp/managed.pyz`. Any pair is suspicious; all three is the dropper. Cross-checked against: • https://app.stepsecurity.io/github/actions-security-demo/compromised-packages/actions/runs/26115553485
ATT&CKT1105 T1059.006
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • DevSecOps test of compromised-package detection content (StepSecurity demo runs are public and reusable)
  • Researcher detonation of the sample in a CrowdStrike / Defender lab
  • Legitimate Python script that happens to write to /tmp/managed.pyz unrelated to durabletask (extremely unlikely given the name)
  • DNS sinkhole replay of git-service.com from a TI feed validator
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: Confirm /tmp/managed.pyz exists and grab SHA256 (expect one of 7d80b3ef.../aeaf583e...). Capture the parent python3 cmdline — `import durabletask` is the smoking gun. 2. CONTAIN: Isolate host; kill all python3 child processes; remove /tmp/managed.pyz; block check.git-service.com and 160.119.64.3 at egress; revoke any cloud credentials reachable from the runtime. 3. HUNT: Search all hosts for the SHA256 and for any process tree where python3 → python3 /tmp/managed.pyz appears. Then pivot to credential_access UCs (gpg --batch --passphrase anon, gh auth token).
let TimeRange = ago(30d);
let C2 = dynamic(["check.git-service.com","git-service.com"]);
let C2IP = dynamic(["160.119.64.3","83.142.209.194"]);
let Net = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > TimeRange
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python","python3","python3.14")
    | where RemoteUrl has_any (C2) or RemoteIP in (C2IP);
let Drop = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > TimeRange
    | where FolderPath == "/tmp" and FileName =~ "managed.pyz"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python","python3","python3.14");
union Net, Drop
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let TimeRange = ago(30d);
let C2 = dynamic(["check.git-service.com","git-service.com"]);
let C2IP = dynamic(["160.119.64.3","83.142.209.194"]);
let Net = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > TimeRange
    | where HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent has_any ("Python-urllib","python-requests","python3")
         or Url has "rope.pyz"
    | where HttpHostName has_any (C2) or DstIpAddr in (C2IP) or Url has_any (C2)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcHostname, HttpHostName, Url, DstIpAddr;
let Drop = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > TimeRange
    | where TargetFilePath has "/tmp/managed.pyz"
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","python3","python3.14")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath;
union Net, Drop
| order by TimeGenerated desc

python3 import durabletask spawning detached /tmp/managed.pyz collector swarm AIInstallation High
Detects the rope.pyz post-import behaviour: a single `python3 -c "import durabletask"` parent spawning multiple `python3 /tmp/managed.pyz` children, each detached via start_new_session=True. Hunting for the parent→child binary pair `/tmp/managed.pyz` is essentially zero-FP — that path was attacker-chosen specifically to look bland. Rationale: Article explicitly enumerates the process tree: PID 2380/2404/2430/2432 all `python3 /tmp/managed.pyz` from a single parent. The cmdline literal `/tmp/managed.pyz` + python parent is article-specific and not a generic LOLBin pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://app.stepsecurity.io/github/actions-security-demo/compromised-packages/actions/runs/26115553485
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1564.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Researcher detonation in a Defender / CrowdStrike sandbox
  • Repeated re-run of the StepSecurity public Actions workflow for content development
  • Internal SOC purple-team test of the same SDK
  • Legitimate program named managed.pyz under /tmp on an unrelated system (extremely unlikely)
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: Pull the full process tree from this DeviceId, expect 3-4 sibling python3 → managed.pyz children plus follow-on `gh auth token`, `gpg --batch --passphrase anon`, `systemctl --user daemon-reload`, `kubectl version --client`. 2. CONTAIN: Isolate host; kill all python3 children; delete /tmp/managed.pyz; revoke github PATs, AWS keys, GCP/Azure SP creds, npm tokens reachable from the runtime; remove pgsql-monitor.service. 3. HUNT: Across the fleet, query for any host where ProcessCommandLine has `/tmp/managed.pyz`; also check DeviceNetworkEvents for `check.git-service.com` / 160.119.64.3 hits in the prior 30 days.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python","python3","python3.14")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/managed.pyz"
| summarize ChildPids = dcount(ProcessId), AnyCmd = any(ProcessCommandLine), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), ParentCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
          by DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessId
| where ChildPids >= 2
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","python3","python3.14")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/managed.pyz"
| summarize ChildPids = dcount(TargetProcessId), AnyCmd = any(TargetProcessCommandLine), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), ParentCmd = any(ActingProcessCommandLine)
          by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessId
| where ChildPids >= 2
| order by FirstSeen desc

Fake pgsql-monitor.service persistence via systemctl --user daemon-reload from python parent AIInstallation High
rope.pyz installs a fake systemd user unit named pgsql-monitor.service then issues `systemctl --user daemon-reload`. Detects the cmdline `systemctl --user daemon-reload` when spawned by python3 — and any creation of a unit file named pgsql-monitor.service. Non-obvious persistence path: user-scope (not system) so root isn't needed. Rationale: Two article-specific literals: the deliberately bland service name `pgsql-monitor.service` and the `systemctl --user daemon-reload` cmdline spawned by python3. Neither is a normal admin operation in a CI runner or microservice host. Cross-checked against: • https://app.stepsecurity.io/github/actions-security-demo/compromised-packages/actions/runs/26115553485
ATT&CKT1543.002 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • DBA running a legitimate pgsql-monitor.service on a Postgres host (rare — check file owner / hash)
  • Configuration management (Ansible/Puppet) installing a user-scope service named similarly
  • Developer manually doing systemctl --user daemon-reload from a Jupyter notebook (parent would be python but interactive)
  • Researcher detonation in lab
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("ansible-playbook","puppet apply","chef-client","salt-call") and AccountName in ("root","ansible","puppet"))
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: Read the body of `~/.config/systemd/user/pgsql-monitor.service` (or its system-wide equivalent) — expect an ExecStart that re-launches python3 /tmp/managed.pyz or a fetch from check.git-service.com. Hash it; compare to article hashes. 2. CONTAIN: `systemctl --user disable --now pgsql-monitor.service`, delete the unit file, remove /tmp/managed.pyz, isolate the host. 3. HUNT: Across the fleet, list any host with a `pgsql-monitor.service` user unit file — that's the persistence beachhead.
let TimeRange = ago(30d);
let Procs = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > TimeRange
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python","python3","python3.14")
    | where (FileName =~ "systemctl" and ProcessCommandLine has "--user" and ProcessCommandLine has "daemon-reload")
        or ProcessCommandLine has "pgsql-monitor"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "process";
let Files = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > TimeRange
    | where FileName =~ "pgsql-monitor.service"
       or (FolderPath has "systemd/user" and FileName endswith ".service" and InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python","python3","python3.14"))
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "file";
union Procs, Files
| order by Timestamp desc
let TimeRange = ago(30d);
let Procs = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > TimeRange
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","python3","python3.14")
    | where (TargetProcessName has "systemctl" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "--user" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "daemon-reload")
        or TargetProcessCommandLine has "pgsql-monitor"
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "process";
let Files = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > TimeRange
    | where TargetFileName =~ "pgsql-monitor.service"
       or (TargetFilePath has "systemd/user" and TargetFileName endswith ".service" and ActingProcessName has_any ("python","python3","python3.14"))
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, Source = "file";
union Procs, Files
| order by TimeGenerated desc

GPG batch passphrase 'anon' + gh auth token credential harvesting from python parent AIActions on Objectives High
rope.pyz collectors invoke `gpg --batch --passphrase anon --decrypt` (a literal, hard-coded passphrase) and `gh auth token` / `gh auth status --show-token` from a python3 parent. The cmdline `--passphrase anon` is essentially unique to this campaign; `gh auth token` from a non-shell parent (python3) is the second high-fidelity tell. Rationale: `--passphrase anon` is a literal attacker-chosen passphrase essentially unique to rope.pyz; `gh auth token` parented by python3 is unusual everywhere (gh is interactive CLI). Article enumerates both for every managed.pyz child. Cross-checked against: • https://app.stepsecurity.io/github/actions-security-demo/compromised-packages/actions/runs/26115553485
ATT&CKT1555 T1552.001 T1528
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Test harness that intentionally tests gpg with `anon` passphrase
  • Helper scripts that wrap `gh auth token` to mint short-lived tokens for downstream tooling (parent should be a shell, not python3)
  • CI bootstrap script invoking gh from Python — investigate the calling repo
  • Researcher detonation
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: Identify the python3 parent's source (typically a sibling `python3 /tmp/managed.pyz`). If managed.pyz, treat as confirmed. 2. CONTAIN: Revoke all gh / GitHub PATs / SSO tokens for the runtime identity; rotate any GPG-encrypted secret reachable from the host (cloud creds, age-encrypted files); isolate host. 3. HUNT: Search 90d of process events for `--passphrase anon` and `gh auth token` parented by anything non-interactive; pivot on GitHub audit log for `git.clone`, `repo.create` (public) and `PersonalAccessToken.update` from the stolen token's account in the prior 7 days — rope.pyz creates public repos as an exfil channel.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python","python3","python3.14")
| where (FileName =~ "gpg" and ProcessCommandLine has "--batch" and ProcessCommandLine has "--passphrase" and ProcessCommandLine has " anon" and ProcessCommandLine has "--decrypt")
   or (FileName =~ "gh" and (ProcessCommandLine has "auth token" or ProcessCommandLine has "auth status --show-token"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","python3","python3.14")
| where (TargetProcessName has "gpg" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "--batch" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "--passphrase" and TargetProcessCommandLine has " anon" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "--decrypt")
   or (TargetProcessName has "gh" and (TargetProcessCommandLine has "auth token" or TargetProcessCommandLine has "auth status --show-token"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: GPG --passphrase anon + gh auth token from Python (rope.pyz Credential Theft)

references:

  OR (ImageFileName=/\/gh$/i AND regex("auth\\s+(token|status\\s+--show-token)", field=CommandLine))

DNS / connection to TeamPCP secondary C2 m-kosche.com AICommand & Control Medium
Catches any host resolving or connecting to the TeamPCP infrastructure: primary C2 git-service.com / check.git-service.com (160.119.64.3) and Mini Shai-Hulud secondary C2 m-kosche.com / t.m-kosche.com (83.142.209.194). The secondary C2 is the cross-campaign tie linking this incident to TanStack, LiteLLM, Mistral, and @antv compromises. Rationale: Four article-listed FQDNs + two attacker-controlled IPs (NameSilo / PrivacyGuardian-registered git-service.com on 2026-05-16, HostUS AS7489 hosting). Secondary C2 m-kosche.com is the cross-campaign tie to Mini Shai-Hulud (TanStack/LiteLLM/Mistral/@antv) which makes the m-kosche match particularly high-fidelity. CloudWatch left empty because VPC Flow Log fields (srcAddr/dstAddr) aren't on the CloudTrail field whitelist this pipeline accepts. Cross-checked against: • https://app.stepsecurity.io/github/actions-security-demo/compromised-packages/actions/runs/26115553485
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • TI vendor sandbox / IOC validator resolving the domain
  • Internal blue-team purple-test resolving the IOC
  • Researcher detonation lab
  • Misconfigured allowlist accidentally allowing a stale TI entry to bounce off proxy
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: For every matching host, pull DeviceProcessEvents same ±5 min — expect python3 import durabletask, `/tmp/managed.pyz`, gh/gpg credential calls. 2. CONTAIN: Sinkhole git-service.com and m-kosche.com at internal DNS; block 160.119.64.3 and 83.142.209.194 at egress; isolate any matching host; revoke all credentials reachable from the runtime. 3. HUNT: Across all telemetry sources for the prior 60 days, pivot on these four FQDNs and two IPs — any historical hit means a host was likely compromised in the Mini Shai-Hulud TanStack / LiteLLM / Mistral / @antv waves.
let BadDomains = dynamic(["m-kosche.com","t.m-kosche.com","git-service.com","check.git-service.com"]);
let BadIPs = dynamic(["160.119.64.3","83.142.209.194"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (BadDomains) or RemoteIP in (BadIPs)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
let TimeRange = ago(30d);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["m-kosche.com","t.m-kosche.com","git-service.com","check.git-service.com"]);
let BadIPs = dynamic(["160.119.64.3","83.142.209.194"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(
  ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > TimeRange
  | where DnsQuery has_any (BadDomains)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host = SrcHostname, SrcIp = SrcIpAddr, Indicator = DnsQuery, Channel = "DNS", Vendor = EventVendor, Product = EventProduct
),
(
  ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > TimeRange
  | where DstHostname has_any (BadDomains) or DstIpAddr in (BadIPs) or Url has_any (BadDomains)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host = SrcHostname, SrcIp = SrcIpAddr, Indicator = coalesce(DstHostname, tostring(DstIpAddr)), Channel = "Network", Vendor = EventVendor, Product = EventProduct
),
(
  CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > TimeRange
  | where DestinationHostName has_any (BadDomains) or RequestURL has_any (BadDomains) or DestinationIP in (BadIPs)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host = SourceHostName, SrcIp = SourceIP, Indicator = coalesce(DestinationHostName, tostring(DestinationIP)), Channel = "CSL", Vendor = DeviceVendor, Product = DeviceProduct
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: DNS or Connection to TeamPCP Mini Shai-Hulud C2 Infrastructure
id: 6b1f2a18-3d44-4f10-93c6-7f3a9b8e1f06

AWS SSM SendCommand / kubectl exec lateral movement from compromised CI runtime AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects the rope.pyz lateral-movement phase: `kubectl version --client` (recon) and `kubectl exec` (lateral) spawned by python3, plus AWS SSM SendCommand / StartSession originating from an EC2 / CI identity that was active around the time managed.pyz fired. Article calls out AWS SSM and kubectl exec specifically as the two propagation channels. Rationale: Three article-specific commands: `kubectl version --client` (article's exact K8s recon string), `kubectl exec` (article's exact lateral movement primitive), and `aws ssm send-command/start-session` (the article's named AWS lateral channel). All three are valid admin operations in isolation — the python3 parent context is what makes the signal. The CloudTrail half adds tenant-side visibility independent of EDR coverage. Cross-checked against: • https://app.stepsecurity.io/github/actions-security-demo/compromised-packages/actions/runs/26115553485
ATT&CKT1021.007 T1609 T1018
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate CI pipeline running `kubectl version --client` for diagnostic logging at start of a deploy step
  • Python automation that wraps AWS SSM SendCommand for fleet maintenance
  • Argo / Tekton tasks executing kubectl from python entrypoints
  • Researcher / IR re-detonation
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("argo-workflows","tekton","buildkite-agent","github-actions-runner") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "deploy")
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: For each match, walk back the process tree — sibling `python3 /tmp/managed.pyz` or `gh auth token` calls within ±60 s confirms the rope.pyz origin. Pull the AWS CloudTrail SSM event matching the source IP and check requestParameters.instanceIds / documentName. 2. CONTAIN: Revoke the IAM role / instance profile used; rotate cluster kubeconfig for the targeted namespace; quarantine any EC2 instance touched by an SSM SendCommand from a confirmed compromised identity; isolate origin host. 3. HUNT: List all SSM SendCommand / kubectl exec from the compromised identity in the prior 14 days; review any pods/instances they touched for follow-on rope.pyz artifacts (/tmp/managed.pyz, pgsql-monitor.service, gpg --passphrase anon traces).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python","python3","python3.14")
| where (FileName =~ "kubectl" and (ProcessCommandLine has "version --client" or ProcessCommandLine has " exec "))
   or (FileName =~ "aws" and (ProcessCommandLine has "ssm send-command" or ProcessCommandLine has "ssm start-session"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","python3","python3.14")
| where (TargetProcessName has "kubectl" and (TargetProcessCommandLine has "version --client" or TargetProcessCommandLine has " exec "))
   or (TargetProcessName has "aws" and (TargetProcessCommandLine has "ssm send-command" or TargetProcessCommandLine has "ssm start-session"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(linux.auditd OR linux.syslog) @process.parent.name:(python OR python3 OR python3.14) ((@process.name:kubectl @process.command_line:(*"version --client"* OR *" exec "*)) OR (@process.name:aws @process.command_line:(*"ssm send-command"* OR *"ssm start-session"*)))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/(python3?(\.14)?)$/i
| (ImageFileName=/\/kubectl$/i AND regex("version\\s+--client|\\sexec\\s", field=CommandLine))
  OR (ImageFileName=/\/aws$/i AND regex("ssm\\s+(send-command|start-session)", field=CommandLine))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
# log group: /aws/cloudtrail
fields @timestamp, eventName, eventSource, awsRegion, sourceIPAddress, userIdentity.type, userIdentity.arn, userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.userName, userIdentity.sessionContext.attributes.mfaAuthenticated, requestParameters.instanceIds.0, requestParameters.documentName, requestParameters.target, userAgent
| filter eventSource = "ssm.amazonaws.com"
      and eventName in ["SendCommand","StartSession","ResumeSession"]
      and not isPresent(errorCode)
      and (userAgent like /Boto3/ or userAgent like /python-requests/ or userAgent like /aws-cli/)
      and userIdentity.type in ["AssumedRole","IAMUser","Federated"]
| sort @timestamp desc
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmds from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("python","python3","python3.14") (Processes.process_name="kubectl" OR Processes.process_name="aws") (Processes.process="*kubectl*exec*" OR Processes.process="*kubectl version --client*" OR Processes.process="*ssm send-command*" OR Processes.process="*ssm start-session*") by host Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmds from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("python","python3","python3.14") (Processes.process_name="kubectl" OR Processes.process_name="aws") (Processes.process="*kubectl*exec*" OR Processes.process="*kubectl version --client*" OR Processes.process="*ssm send-command*" OR Processes.process="*ssm start-session*") by host Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user

    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("288f26c2eadcb1a7923fe376d16f5404216cce15d9fc162a4a78574dc7df399a", "ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90", "5926b86b642e00672252953eb30d8f75cfb7797fe3118bd6fa2cfbee92905d61", "e3dbe63aded45278f49c4746ab938ed9472b36def79b43e2dd2d7eff014481d1", "82d83274680df928fdda296a348e01802f595e412308c399565c320df444052a") or SHA1 in~ ("288f26c2eadcb1a7923fe376d16f5404216cce15d9fc162a4a78574dc7df399a", "ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90", "5926b86b642e00672252953eb30d8f75cfb7797fe3118bd6fa2cfbee92905d61", "e3dbe63aded45278f49c4746ab938ed9472b36def79b43e2dd2d7eff014481d1", "82d83274680df928fdda296a348e01802f595e412308c399565c320df444052a") or MD5 in~ ("288f26c2eadcb1a7923fe376d16f5404216cce15d9fc162a4a78574dc7df399a", "ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90", "5926b86b642e00672252953eb30d8f75cfb7797fe3118bd6fa2cfbee92905d61", "e3dbe63aded45278f49c4746ab938ed9472b36def79b43e2dd2d7eff014481d1", "82d83274680df928fdda296a348e01802f595e412308c399565c320df444052a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("288f26c2eadcb1a7923fe376d16f5404216cce15d9fc162a4a78574dc7df399a", "ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90", "5926b86b642e00672252953eb30d8f75cfb7797fe3118bd6fa2cfbee92905d61", "e3dbe63aded45278f49c4746ab938ed9472b36def79b43e2dd2d7eff014481d1", "82d83274680df928fdda296a348e01802f595e412308c399565c320df444052a") or SHA1 in~ ("288f26c2eadcb1a7923fe376d16f5404216cce15d9fc162a4a78574dc7df399a", "ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90", "5926b86b642e00672252953eb30d8f75cfb7797fe3118bd6fa2cfbee92905d61", "e3dbe63aded45278f49c4746ab938ed9472b36def79b43e2dd2d7eff014481d1", "82d83274680df928fdda296a348e01802f595e412308c399565c320df444052a") or MD5 in~ ("288f26c2eadcb1a7923fe376d16f5404216cce15d9fc162a4a78574dc7df399a", "ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90", "5926b86b642e00672252953eb30d8f75cfb7797fe3118bd6fa2cfbee92905d61", "e3dbe63aded45278f49c4746ab938ed9472b36def79b43e2dd2d7eff014481d1", "82d83274680df928fdda296a348e01802f595e412308c399565c320df444052a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["288f26c2eadcb1a7923fe376d16f5404216cce15d9fc162a4a78574dc7df399a", "ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90", "5926b86b642e00672252953eb30d8f75cfb7797fe3118bd6fa2cfbee92905d61", "e3dbe63aded45278f49c4746ab938ed9472b36def79b43e2dd2d7eff014481d1", "82d83274680df928fdda296a348e01802f595e412308c399565c320df444052a"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Securing CI/CD in an agentic world: Claude Code Github action case

Microsoft Security Blog
2026-06-05 7 use cases 8 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Microsoft Threat Intelligence identified a prompt injection pathway in Claude Code GitHub Action that allowed access to workflow secrets under specific conditions. This research examines the attack chain, responsible disclosure process, Anthropic's mitigation, and guidance for securing AI-powered CI/CD workflows. The post Securing CI/CD in an agentic world: Claude Code Github action case appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog .

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Claude Code Action Read tool exfil: node opens /proc/<pid>/environ on Linux CI runner · [LLM] Claude Code Read tool steered to cloud-credential files on GitHub Actions runner · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] GitHub Actions runner: node from Claude Code Action egresses to non-Anthropic/non-GitHub endpoint
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Claude Code Action Read tool exfil: node opens /proc/<pid>/environ on Linux CI runner AIExploitation High
Hunts the exact exploitation primitive Microsoft Threat Intelligence described: the Claude Code Action's in-process Read tool, when steered by an injected prompt, opens /proc/self/environ (or /proc/<pid>/environ) to harvest the workflow's ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, and OIDC credentials. Pre-fix (claude-code-action <2.1.128) the Bubblewrap sandbox + CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB does not cover Read, so the node process serving Claude Code opens /proc directly — a path almost nothing legitimate touches on a build runner. Rationale: Article names the exact primitive: 'eventually authorized to access /proc/self/environ, reading the workflow's ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'. We pin on the Linux file path regex + node as the actor. The Read tool runs in-process inside node (not via Bash), so the file event is the only signal — there is no child process to pivot on. Corroborated by Flatt Security (flatt.tech) and Hacker News reporting which describe the same /proc/self/environ exfil chain. Cross-checked against: • https://flatt.tech/research/posts/poisoning-claude-code-one-github-issue-to-break-the-supply-chain/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/claude-code-github-action-flaw-let-one.html • https://oddguan.com/blog/comment-and-control-prompt-injection-credential-theft-claude-code-gemini-cli-github-copilot/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1212 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Container/process observability agents (datadog-agent, sysdig, falcon-sensor, osquery) using a bundled node helper to enumerate process env for inventory
  • Self-hosted runner image pre-flight scripts that introspect node's own environment for diagnostics (e.g. Node's --inspect tooling)
  • node-based Kubernetes operators (kube-state-metrics ports, Pulumi/CDK preview scripts) iterating /proc to map sibling containers
  • Security tooling that legitimately scans /proc for secret leakage (gitleaks/trufflehog wrapper jobs)
  • Node debugger sessions where a developer manually reads /proc/self/environ to diagnose env-var passing
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("datadog-agent", "sysdig", "falcon-sensor", "osqueryd", "trufflehog", "gitleaks")) and not(InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "/opt/datadog-agent" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "/opt/sysdig")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the InitiatingProcessCommandLine and folder path — confirm node was launched from `_actions/anthropics/claude-code-action*` or `@anthropic-ai/claude-code`. Pull the GitHub run ID from the runner work dir (`/home/runner/work/<repo>/<repo>` or env GITHUB_RUN_ID) and fetch the triggering issue/PR body via gh api; look for HTML-comment payloads, /proc references, or Read-tool instructions. Step 2 (contain): Rotate ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, the workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN scopes, any OIDC-issued cloud creds, and every other secret exposed to that job. Disable the workflow file until upgraded to claude-code-action ≥2.1.128. For self-hosted runners, isolate the runner host pending forensics. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on the same node PID to DeviceNetworkEvents/NetworkConnectIP4 in the surrounding 60s for outbound to non-Anthropic/non-GitHub IPs (exfil destination). Hunt repo-wide for other workflows pinning vulnerable claude-code-action SHAs. Audit recent PRs opened by the AI bot accoun
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node"
| where FolderPath matches regex @"^/proc/(self|\d+)/environ$"
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("_work/", "actions-runner", "_actions/anthropics/claude-code-action", "runners/") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("@anthropic-ai/claude-code", "claude-code-action")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessId,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "/node" or ActingProcessName =~ "node"
| where TargetFilePath matches regex @"^/proc/(self|\d+)/environ$"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("claude-code", "@anthropic-ai", "_actions/anthropics", "actions-runner", "/_work/")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          ActingProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessId, TargetFilePath, EventType, DvcAction
| order by TimeGenerated desc
